detail: T-CMD LIST on persvati cores 12-23, tmpfs, scale-1m, one client, a 2-group LIST. Before (dev f2629613e): p50 1.15 s / 11.3 s / 29.0 s at 1k / 10k / 25k articles, owner CPU 58 / 820 / 3,086 ms. After (lane/list-walk@42ef30e71, L): p50/p99 0.41/2.50 ms at 1k, 0.47/2.65 ms at 10k, 0.41/5.95 ms at 25k; owner CPU 0.57-0.67 ms per LIST, flat (bar p99 <= 50 ms, exponent <= 0.2: PASS). Raw: persvati:/tank/fn/scratch/load-harness/runs/lw2-tcmd-*. Mechanisms: (A) fn-lst was a one-step def-cursor, one controller call per host activation, each empty yield paced by a 1 ms delay; now fn-lst-batch (def-cursor/batch) spends the visit grant and fn-asto-resume-ms (ACL2) makes a LIST yield due on the next loop pass. (B) the :summary phase probed every article number of a group; now the summary is fn-scat-available-summary, the catalog's carried live count/low/high corrected over rows appended or withdrawn since the captured view, read in one call per group. Statements: fn-lst-step-residual / fn-lst-batch-residual, fn-asto-resume-ms-lst-is-immediate, fn-asto-resume-ms-over-waits (teeth in article-stream-owner-teeth-tests), fn-scat-available-summary-is-the-walk (carried summary = numbered walk when the group high is below the watermark), fn-lst-groups-reference-is-active-lines/-counts-lines (premise-free), fn-lst-one-finite-progress (re-proved). books/group-summary-cursor is deleted. Lands with the next train.
